name: Arteriocyte Magellan

card.summary: A clinic centrifuge system for preparing platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from a patient's own blood, used in PRP treatments for hair and skin.
card.note: A clinic device; PRP for hair and skin is used off label and results vary.

quick.overview:
The Arteriocyte Magellan is a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) separation system: a machine that spins a sample of a patient's blood to concentrate platelets for application at a treatment site. In appearance medicine, PRP is used for hair thinning and skin rejuvenation.

The system was first cleared by the FDA in 2002 under Medtronic and is now marketed by Arteriocyte Medical Systems for blood and bone marrow concentrates in surgical settings. Studies of PRP in general report mixed results.
quick.how: In clinic use, blood is drawn, processed in the device and the concentrate is injected or applied, often with microneedling for skin. Hair protocols commonly involve a series of sessions spaced weeks apart followed by maintenance.
quick.risks: Risks relate to the procedure: injection-site pain and bruising, and infection control. A 2024 CDC report linked HIV cases to an unlicensed spa that reused contaminated equipment during vampire-facial procedures.

lead: The Arteriocyte Magellan Autologous Platelet Separator System is a device for preparing platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from a patient's own blood. PRP is a concentrate that keeps platelets, which carry growth factors, and removes most red blood cells.[1][4]

In cosmetic practice PRP is used for androgenetic and other hair loss, and for wrinkles, fine lines and skin rejuvenation, including combination with microneedling in so-called vampire facials.[1] Wikipedia notes that the PRP itself is not FDA-regulated and is used off label, while devices that prepare it require clearance.[1]

The Magellan was cleared by the FDA on 12 August 2002 under a Medtronic applicant, using Harvest Technologies' SmartPReP centrifuge as its predicate, and is now the lead product of Arteriocyte Medical Systems of Hopkinton, Massachusetts, which describes it as a closed system able to produce a platelet concentrate from blood or bone marrow in about fifteen minutes.[2][3][4]

chain: Blood drawn and spun in a separator
Injected into scalp or skin for thicker-looking hair or better skin
angle.text: The device is the preparation step for PRP treatments that clinics offer for hair thinning and skin rejuvenation. It turns a small blood draw into a platelet concentrate at the point of care.

infobox: Preparation of platelet-poor plasma and platelet concentrate from a small blood sample[4]

paras: Magellan is described by its maker as an autologous platelet separator system, with disposable kits and a benchtop centrifuge, intended for the rapid production of platelet-rich plasma from blood and bone marrow.[2][3] The company says its bone marrow technology concentrates aspirated marrow in a closed system in the operating room, giving a product rich in platelets and stem cells in as little as fifteen minutes, and says it focuses on cardiac, orthopedic and vascular surgery.[2][3]
In June 2012 the FDA approved Arteriocyte's own brand of ACD-A anticoagulant solution for use with the system, packaged in single-use 50 cc units that replaced 30 cc vials in its surgical kits.[2][3]

The FDA record for K021902 lists the Magellan Autologous Platelet Separator System and disposable kit as substantially equivalent on 12 August 2002, with Medtronic named as applicant. Its indication is the safe and rapid preparation of platelet-poor plasma and platelet concentrate from a small blood sample, in a clinical laboratory or at the point of care during surgery.[4] The listed predicate was the SmartPReP centrifuge system from Harvest Technologies.[4]
Blood is centrifuged, often in two stages, to concentrate platelets to roughly three to five times normal levels. Preparations are classified by leukocyte and fibrin content.[1]

PRP is used for hair loss, with courses often starting with about three monthly treatments, and for skin rejuvenation, including with microneedling.[1] Wikipedia notes that the PRP preparation is used off label and that devices require FDA clearance.[1]
No studies found for this device specifically. Studies of PRP in general report mixed results, with some support for hair loss and joint use.[1]

timeline.event: Harvest Technologies' SmartPReP system cleared, later cited as the Magellan's predicate.[4]
FDA 510(k) clearance of the Magellan system on 12 August.[4]
Arteriocyte Medical Systems created through a partnership with DW Healthcare Partners and Comerica.[2]
FDA approves Arteriocyte's own ACD-A solution for use with Magellan, 4 June.[2][3]
